Adversaries of Adagím
You have defeated Shálith
Track down and defeat every formidable enemy in Adagím.

Upon observing the deadly sharpness of this creature's stinger, the Kintai of Sul Madásh named it Shálith, which means \qcut of the scythe\q in their tongue. Now it has fallen to the reaper and will trouble them no longer.

Lankier than many of his kind, Strákhal the Strangler had always been sickly and possessed of a sour disposition that made him unwelcome in the camps of other Orcs. He looked weak, but his hands were very, very strong.

The Kintai of Sul Madásh did not know how many years Thagára spent hunting near the Elderwell, but they believe its crushing maw may have endangered even the long-vanished Ishâkhai who once dwelt there. Thagára's opinion on the subject was not known.

Sóthadar the Trickster grew to tremendous size and stood taller than many of the other creatures that stalked the fens of Adagím. Kintai reported seeing Sóthadar in many places at once, which seems impossible but not out of the question for such a master of deceit as this fungus-covered troublemaker.
For many months the jackal Âkhtal crept on silent feet through the blighted woods of Adagím, preying on travellers in that unhappy land. Now his despoiling days are done.

Hórush Hollow-heart peacefully haunted the Hill of the Mother for many years, but as the blight worsened in Adagím so too did its disposition. To Irsinith's great sorrow, Hórush showed no sign of recovering its former calm.

Spiders throughout Middle-earth delight in preying upon the weak and the unwary, but those like Lhálach, stricken by the blight, can prove even more deadly and unpredictable. The Kintai will shed no tears for Lhálach, though they understand the creature may have been a victim in its own right.

The Kintai of Sul Madásh reported seeing the shadow of a woman creeping among the blighted trees of Adagím. You have learned her identity and ended her mission all at once, and Caelgeth the plague-seeker will no longer disturb the Kintai.
Agáthar was both old and powerful, but none now but he remember what he had lost.

Enemies of An Shêru
You have defeated Enudâri
Track down and defeat every formidable enemy in An Shêru.

Enudâri was a great Shagâni warrior long ago, and his legend only grew in the centuries since his death. He stalked the high-lands as a wight, animated by evil forces and sent against the fearful folk of An Shêru, until you ended Enudâri's second legend.

'Some men work with silver, and design fashionable candlesticks. Some men bake delicious loaves of bread. Some men prepare cuts of steak to sell at market. Têzdab the Butcher did none of these things. Let us leave it at that.' -Merchant Dejemûl

Fer-nefâsi came out of the northern skies with a terrible thunderclap, and nested near to Jiret-menêsh. The Temámir insist they did not seal the doors from fear of the enormous creature, but neither have they convincingly denied it.
Biret-kôda was known for its foul temper and its iron-like hide, and for the sound of its hooves as it charged toward any who strayed too near its territory.

'Gilkharkûn has been known to attack travellers along the ridge, and if the fight goes badly it sheds its tail and escapes! I know not how it learned to do this, but I have seen it first-hand! I tried selling the tail but nobody wanted it. Eventually I just got rid of the thing, for it had started to smell.' -Merchant Dejemûl
You have seen to it that Lipûzu's days of cracking bones and sucking out the marrow within are ended. The slain kergrim may now sate the appetite of his brothers and sisters.

Any of the kalorkhûn were to be avoided, but Úmgi Shearspur was more dangerous than most. Some of the Temámir refused to travel on foot outside Jiret-menêsh because the terrifying birds could outrun them. You have done well to rid An Shêru of this threat.
Adâzi the Scather may be gone, but the terrible corpse-like stench that surrounded her still burns your nose. Yuck!
Daithor of the Utûgi roved across the Height of the Sky in the company of a band of deadly warriors in search of helpless folk to seize and bring to his masters.

Ekal-nêbi, the Fallen Palace -- Tier 1

The palace of Ekal-nêbi is the crown jewel of Emax Dûl, an opulent home to rulers from the kingdom of Nêshak, Nísaka... and now from Ordâkh. Hidden in the background of palace life, Thothril the Entangler, Thardúth of Damudûr, quietly began working her enchantments upon the minds of its inhabitants. Now with soldiers of Mizâdi's alliance at the palace doorstep, she asserts final control over the palace.

In the forgotten caves of Hurum Kâna, a scoundrel makes his home. The self-styled brigand king, Bârlat the Bold strikes at caravans and travellers on the nearby Great Road. The Doorwards of Zajâna have tasked you with bringing Bârlat to justice. But what secrets could the caves - and Bârlat - be hiding, deep in Hurum Kâna?

Overlooking Damudûr, Kôth Rau serves as stronghold for those who wish to subjugate the peoples of An Shêru. Faeron and Rhadrog have tasked you with entering this stronghold and defeating the sorceress Ombátha and the cruel Utûgi leader, Râkdakul. The hope is that with the defeat of these cruel masters, it will break the hold on those under their influence.

The palace of Ekal-nêbi is the crown jewel of Emax Dûl, an opulent home to rulers from the kingdom of Nêshak, Nísaka... and now from Ordâkh. Hidden in the background of palace life, Thothril the Entangler, Thardúth of Damudûr, quietly began working her enchantments upon the minds of its inhabitants. Now with soldiers of Mizâdi's alliance at the palace doorstep, she asserts final control over the palace.

For over a hundred years, the Kintai Elves have battled a mysterious blight, seemingly brought on by the Din of Stone. It has already consumed once-beautiful Adagím, and now threatens the rest of the Elven glades. An investigation by the Rangers Faeron and Rhadrog has tracked the source of the blight to The Folly of Nagakhêdi, but what dangers lurk inside the ancient and abandoned wonder?

Good folk abandoned Mûl Erebu; now it is given over only to scorpions and to those who thought to make use of them, to their sorrow.

Bolo Thúki is the northernmost of the three primary encampments seized by Bârshud's Ordâkhai as they fled south. Here his soldiers attempt to fortify the hillside and make use of the supplies they stole from the village of Hanamíku before the Hamâti army caught up to them.

This is the second of the primary encampments seized by Bârshud's Ordâkhai as they fled into Pahar Hatokáli. Here they keep many of the lions they intend to unleash upon Mizâdi's forces, but the training has not gone entirely smoothly....

The fortress of Imizíla, \qlast torch\q in the Shagâni language, has appropriately become the final bastion for Bârshud's Ordâkhai in Pahar Hatokáli. Trapped between the pursuing forces of Shâra Mizâdi and the raging waters of the Hatokáli River, Imizíla will by necessity be where this army of Ordâkh fights to the end.

The zizani of Ukh-bâra fill the moist air with the sound of their call, and the underbrush rustles as they move hither and yon on skittering legs. Water splashes nearby but you cannot identify the precise location, and you feel insect eyes upon you.
This marshy stretch beside the Hatokáli River is full of life. You are eager to leave it behind.

The caverns of Mut-hûru are actually two cave systems, joined through burrowing activity by underground dwellers beneath the Ridge of Plenty. Tombs of the dead, long abandoned by any save kergrim scavengers, stand within the vast and maze-like caverns.
The alap-nâri oxen dwell at Bûlkharar, beside the Hatokáli River. The atmosphere here is warm and smells of damp hair; an unpleasant combination, though the alap-nâri do not seem to mind.

Old-timers in the village of Hanamíku will tell you that there have always been trouble-makers on the hills above the village, and they would be right: before the brigands, Kakidûr was home to Ordâkhai deserters before they moved on. Remnants of the Ordâkhai presence can still be found there, but most of their equipment has been reclaimed and repurposed by local brigands.

The Orcs of Roz Káskrauz are war-like and aggressive, and while they prefer to remain within their stronghold, they will emerge from it to do battle if they believe they have the upper hand. Until then, they are willing to let the Ordâkhai under Bârshud give their lives as the Hamâti soldiers advance.

The great bridge of Shûmadir has fallen into disrepair over the years. Unless it is repaired, no army can easily pass this way.

The farm of Kirzâmur was burned by the retreating Ordâkhai as they passed south, hoping to prevent its use by Mizâdi's forces. Now Ebnûr and Namtâru seek to maintain a cheerful disposition while they rebuild... easier for the father than it is for his son.
Though long-abandoned by their builders, the water-wheels of Nar Makâru turn still. For what purpose do they now run, and on behalf of what commander?

The forces of Renewed Hamât have established the war camp of Ingarûma on a naturally rocky rise midway through Pahar Hatokáli. Many throughout the years have sought to establish camps here for the commanding view it provides of the surrounding fells. Will Shâra Mizâdi be the last?
Soldiers, provisioners, forge-masters, strategists, and scouts have made this their outpost in lands far from their homes. Most are eager to put an end to Bârshud and the forces he commands so they may leave this place, but until that day comes they will endure.

Little is remembered today of the tower of Sakhar Kishâsya, save that it was built long ago and is more ancient than the other structures in Pahar Hatokáli. It has sunk into the earth as a result of the Din of Stone and other, even older geologic events.
In the Nêshakari tongue, Pagru-kirít means \qGarden of Corpses.\q Perhaps that is enough to know of this place to which only the desperate should come willingly.

The Gates of Eshkhâbul prevent passage further north and west, keeping the brigands that encamp upon the southern slope of Mûr Ghala from leaving and troubling other lands. This is of little comfort to the villagers of nearby Hanamíku, but they were not consulted by those who shut the gates.
The sound booms in your ears as the Hatokáli River descends in an overwhelming torrent, rushing downstream with tremendous voice.
The small graveyard of Khabur Pâshu stands beneath the village of Hanamíku and has served as the final resting place of its people since the village was founded.

The village of Hanamíku serves as a way-station nestled among the rocks of Nêr Abatu, the Gate of Stones that stands between Idagâl and Pahar Hatokáli. It has been a place of peace during the years since the Ordâkhai came north and took up residence at Emax Dûl, but that has changed almost overnight.
Soldiers of Ordâkh fleeing the city passed through Hanamíku on their way south, pursued by the army of Renewed Hamât. Bârshud's forces burned farms and wrought devastation as they fled, seeking to deprive Shâra Mizâdi of help and supplies. Now the villagers fear any who bear weapons, and many mistrust outsiders.
